errors.says: The planned bombing point is assigned 19:50 UTC and 2,500 ft, and the next planned turn 20:25 UTC and 3,500 ft; both complete points have quality=derived and cite s1. The build note calls the planned legs real geometry without explaining these invented timing and height values.
errors.should_be: Only the planned horizontal coordinates can be derived from finding 2, subject to the stated nautical-mile assumption. Treat both timed scene points as modelled and explicitly identify their timestamps and altitudes as illustrative, or leave those values unknown. The cited finding supplies neither waypoint arrival times nor those altitudes.
errors.evidence: s1, finding 2, PDF p.295, prescribes the departure datum, true courses and distances, with low-level bombing but no numerical bombing altitude or waypoint schedule. Cox testimony, printed p.22/PDF p.342, reports 2,300 and 4,500 ft during later, incompletely timed radio exchanges; Exhibit 8, PDF p.38, logs angles 3.5 at 1626R/21:26 UTC. None establishes the two depicted waypoint time/altitude pairs.

errors.says: The HF/DF area is drawn with a radius of exactly 185,200 metres and described simply as within 100 miles; the build note calls it real geometry.
errors.should_be: Disclose that the drawn radius assumes 100 nautical miles. The inspected primary records print only 100 miles, so the exact metric radius is an interpretation, not a verified conversion. Preserve the approximate evaluated-area wording and avoid implying a guaranteed containment boundary. If statute miles were intended, the radius would be 160,934.4 metres instead.
errors.evidence: s1, finding 28/PDF p.298 and Exhibit 11/PDF p.223, give an approximate HF/DF area centred on 29°15′N 79°00′W with radius 100 miles, without expanding the unit. Evaluator testimony, printed pp.51–52/PDF pp.371–372, describes bearings too imprecise for an exact fix and an area for searching. The centre converts correctly to 29.25, -79; the silent choice of nautical miles is what is unsupported.

notes: Checked 154 field/event assertions, including repeated values at separate publication locations: date 1; people including breakdowns 15; aircraft specifications/configuration 11 and member values 20; site conclusion 1; route endpoint/waypoint/leg values 24; numbers entries 13; one_line/status_why 2; event source/time/detail bundles 52; perspectives 5; scene add/overlay/buildNote/endTitle bundles 8; menu label 1; time basis 1. All 52 events were reviewed, exceeding the requested 15. All event quote fields are null, and no other verbatim quotation was found in the research or Flight 19 scene block; no quotation wording or speaker correction is therefore reported. Downloaded the original 549-page Navy PDF and recognition manual with curl; read NARA page OCR and inspected original rendered pages for the roster, weather forms, HF/DF chart and aircraft recognition, plus both later Navy letter images. The operational R-to-UTC conversion is +5 hours, explicitly printed on the contemporary weather forms; the checked conversions, including midnight date changes, agree. Recalculated all four rhumb-line waypoint results under the explicitly disclosed nautical-mile assumption; the rounded coordinates agree. Checked the reported coordinate conversions for both bases, HF/DF centre, inland radar report and probable Mariner flame area. The five perspectives distinguish original Board opinion, the 1947 correction, withdrawn wreck identification, fringe speculation and probable Mariner loss; no additional source-verified fairness error was found. The 1947 letter disapproves blame and states unknown cause; its continuation and final approval papers were not supplied by that image, but the 1960 Navy letter confirms the outcome. The approximately 1500R bombing-completion event is correctly attributed to the secondary NARA history, rather than independently established by the inspected primary finding. Museum aircraft dimensions remain type-level specifications, with the documented variant conflicts. No passenger is named and no gratuitous material was found. Taylor and Powers, the named lost-flight personnel in narrative text, are pilots in the primary roster. Crew/passenger counts use the dataset's disclosed classification of military aircrew trainees; the Board itself calls some aircrew passengers. The Flight 19 direct.js block has no eventTimes override; all its cited IDs exist and refer to s1. The explicitly modelled remaining add points do not claim measured aircraft positions. The menu label and Not found end title agree with the inspected records and recovery-status sources. All 18 listed source URLs were checked, representing 13 unique base URLs. Twelve base URLs returned HTTP 200 with curl, including both PDFs and both Navy letter images. Smithsonian s12 returned HTTP 403 to curl but its complete article resolved through the web reader, so it is access-filtered, not a dead link. No confirmed later recovery announcement was found in the supplementary search; this is not proof that every archive was exhausted. Research files were not edited.
